introduction: Today we celebrate the Ascension of the Lord. Forty days after his Resurrection, Jesus is taken up into heaven. On a mountain in Galilee, he sends his disciples to make disciples of all nations, baptizing and teaching, and promises, I am with you always, until the end of the age. Paul prays that we may know the hope of our calling. Let us lift our eyes to Christ in glory, and then go out as his witnesses.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, all authority in heaven and on earth has been given to Christ. Let us bring him our prayers.
intentions: For the Church: that she may make disciples of all nations, baptizing and teaching all that Christ commanded. Let us pray to the Lord.
For missionaries and catechists: that the Lord may be with them always. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who doubt, as some of the disciples did: that they may still follow and worship the Lord. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who feel alone: that they may know Christ's promise, I am with you always. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that the eyes of our hearts may be enlightened to know the hope of our calling. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Almighty Father, your Son has ascended to your right hand and promised to be with us always. Fill us with hope, and send us out as his witnesses to all nations. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: I am with you always
reflection.body:
For forty days after Easter, Jesus appeared to his apostles and spoke to them about God's Kingdom. Now the time has come for him to return to the Father. In the Acts of the Apostles, he promises them the Holy Spirit: "You will be witnesses to me in Jerusalem, in all Judea and Samaria, and to the uttermost parts of the earth." Then "he was taken up, and a cloud received him out of their sight." Two men in white ask the apostles why they are staring at the sky: Jesus will return, and in the meantime they have work to do.

Matthew ends his Gospel on a mountain in Galilee. The eleven disciples see the risen Jesus and worship him, "but some doubted." Even at this moment, faith and doubt live side by side. Jesus does not send away those who doubt. He comes to them and speaks to all of them.

His words sum up the mission of the Church: "All authority has been given to me in heaven and on earth. Go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, teaching them to observe all things that I commanded you."

And then the promise that ends Matthew's Gospel: "Behold, I am with you always, even to the end of the age." At the beginning of the Gospel, Jesus was called Emmanuel, God with us. At the end, he promises to remain with us. The Ascension is not his absence; it is a new way of being present.

Paul prays that we may know "what is the hope of his calling" and the greatness of God's power, the same power that raised Christ and seated him at God's right hand.

This week, remember that Christ is with you always. And think of one person to whom you could speak about your faith.
